main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating pattern of darker clumps and light speckles; no standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain tile, no standing object; column scan shows only mid green #628433 with occasional 1px lighter #7c9c42 specks)
evidence: Terrain ground tile, not a standing object. It is a flat, uniform surface seen from above, with no top/front structure to judge, so the 3/4 contract does not apply. The kind 'terrain' matches the grass patch. Nothing in it breaks the contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours in the grass reference. Its grass ramp is a mid green with one lighter and one darker green plus a darkest accent, about 3 steps against the reference's 5-6. The tiny tufts, checker speckles and dark blobs repeat in an obvious tiling pattern and are sparse. The base is mostly one flat mid green, though 5x5 flat-fill coverage is only 7%. It has no outline, which is fine for ground. Overall it is far thinner and more repetitive than the Beodeul grass, which has varied clumps and grain.
